gbm_population_evidence.quote: Brain Tumor - Metastatic; Brain Tumor, Adult: Glioblastoma

candidate_evidence.quote: The aim of the study is to compare the effects of continuous 3% hypertonic saline (HS), bolus HS and 20% mannitol on intraoperative brain relaxation in patients with raised intracranial pressure during surgery for supratentorial tumors.

role_evidence.quote: [ACTIVE_COMPARATOR] %3 HS bolus 3 mL.kg-1: After the head fixation 3 mL.kg-1 %3 hypertonic saline will be administered over the 20 min intravenously.
Hyperosmotic agents are used to decrease intracranial pressure.

agents.drug_class_hint: 3% hypertonic saline, hyperosmotic agent for intracranial pressure

role_evidence.quote: [ACTIVE_COMPARATOR] %3 HS infusion 20 ml/h: After the head fixation 3% hypertonic saline at 20 ml/h infusion rate will be administered during the operation

agents.drug_class_hint: 3% hypertonic saline, hyperosmotic agent for intracranial pressure

role_evidence.quote: [ACTIVE_COMPARATOR] %20 mannitol 0,6 gr.kg-1: After the head fixation %20 mannitol 0,6 gr.kg-1 will be administered over the 20 min intravenously.

agents.drug_class_hint: osmotic diuretic for intracranial pressure / brain relaxation

coder_notes: Registered phase NA (fails S3); coded in full. Perioperative anaesthesia trial comparing hyperosmotic agents for brain relaxation; no antitumour hypothesis. All three arms are registered ACTIVE_COMPARATOR, so agents coded control_comparator by rule 1 (first applicable rule); supportive (rule 2) would be the substantive alternative. Population is glioblastoma multiforme or metastatic brain tumours, coded basket_gbm_eligible (multi-cancer, GBM named in conditions and inclusion); mixed_glioma_gbm_named is not apt as no other glioma types. Treatment setting not stated (resection, likely mostly newly diagnosed). Mannitol here is for ICP, not BBB disruption, so not delivery-enabling.
